report:
Reviewed the complete meta.reviews.selector_line_range claim, the sole ordinary implementation association in crates/sage-meta/src/review.rs, and the complete sole ordinary associated test whole_files_and_ranges_preserve_exact_line_endings_and_detect_selected_edits. No TODO/N/A entries exist.

Implementation completeness: select reads the source and splits with split_inclusive('\n'), so line boundaries are newline-delimited and the original CRLF/LF terminators remain part of each selected line. Concatenating lines[start - 1..end] implements one-based inclusive bounds without normalizing whitespace or inventing a final newline. start == 0, end < start, and end > lines.len() reject zero, reversed, and out-of-bounds input before indexing; an end of zero is rejected through these predicates too. An empty file has no selectable lines, and a terminated final line does not create a phantom line. capture_read persists the original Selector::LineRange and source_lines preserves exact bytes through split/join on newline. input_errors resolves each additional fragment using the saved selector and compares reconstructed text exactly, so the saved numeric boundaries are reused; shifting content into or out of them can conservatively stale the review. These behaviors and supporting functions are all in the captured implementation file.

Test adequacy: the associated test creates mixed-terminator text first\r\n\r\nthird\nlast, asserts the exact first two lines including the second line terminator, and asserts the one-line final range equals last with no added newline. Its invalid-range cases (0,1), (3,2), (1,5), and (5,5) cover zero, reversal, end overflow, and wholly outside the file. After recording these numeric ranges it edits only the unselected third line and asserts the check remains valid, then edits selected text and asserts invalidity. Those assertions exercise saved-boundary freshness; source inspection establishes why moving text across a saved boundary is likewise compared as changed text, without requiring identity-based tracking. The remainder of the same test checks repeated whole-file reads, exact serialization reconstruction and final-newline staleness, which is consistent adjacent evidence rather than a separate range guarantee. Fixture helpers were captured (tests/review.rs lines 1-105): they create an isolated workspace, write exact strings, call real start/record APIs, and deserialize saved input. Captured check/lib portions establish that the is_valid assertions include the real review stage and its validation result. No essential line-selection behavior lives outside the associated implementation file.
